label: About
headline: Engineer first, measured second
intro: I build production web apps across the whole stack — TypeScript on React/Next.js and Angular at the front, Node.js and NestJS behind it, deployed on GCP and Cloudflare. Three years in, most of that time inside product teams shipping to real users.

What I care about is the part after merge: whether the change moved a number, what it cost to run, and what it will cost the next person to maintain. I read dashboards as often as I read pull requests.

facts.label: Languages
facts.value: English C1 reading/listening, B2 speaking (EF SET) · Ukrainian, Russian native

principles.label: How I work

items.title: End-to-end ownership
items.body: Comfortable taking a feature from architecture decision through database schema, API, frontend, CI/CD and post-release monitoring. Shipping means it's live and observed, not merged.

items.title: Decisions backed by data
items.body: Product analytics and feature flags as part of the normal workflow. Ran 7+ A/B experiments on conversion funnels rather than shipping on intuition.

items.title: AI-assisted workflow
items.body: Custom prompts and context setups built into daily development to cut boilerplate and accelerate delivery — a deliberate process, not an occasional tool.

principles.note: Day to day that runs inside structured Agile workflows — Jira-tracked planning, code review, iterative delivery — and usually alongside a designer, working from the same files rather than across a handoff.

entries.title: Starting computer science in Zaporizhzhia
entries.body: Enrolled at the Polytechnic National University with no real code behind me. The first year was algorithms on paper and C++ in a lab, and the first thing that stuck was how much faster I learned when I had something to ship.

entries.title: A puzzle game in Unity, released to strangers
entries.body: Built a small puzzle game in Unity over a few months and put it out publicly. It taught me more about scope and finishing than any course did — most of the work turned out to be the last ten percent.

entries.title: Internship at GroupBWT
entries.body: First time working inside a real process: Jira tickets, code review, a mentor reading everything I wrote. Shipped features across frontend, backend and admin panel, and learned to size work honestly.

entries.title: Binary Studio Academy
entries.body: Three months of full stack work at an uncomfortable pace: React, Express, Docker, WebSockets, tests expected rather than optional. The habit of writing code someone else will review started here.

entries.title: Joining a product team at Coverr
entries.body: Moved from building features to owning them: an Angular and NestJS microservice platform with paying users, analytics on every funnel, and infrastructure decisions with a monthly bill attached.

entries.title: Moving to Varna
entries.body: Relocated to the Bulgarian coast and settled into remote work across European time zones. Same job, quieter mornings, and a commute that ends at the sea instead of a metro station.

now.label: Now
now.heading: Based in Varna, Bulgaria
now.body: Working remotely on EET, which overlaps comfortably with most European teams and part of the US morning. Available for a new role from September 2026 — full-time remote, ideally on a product with real users and real numbers to move.
